description: Output quality eval: verify ue-dev-cycle produces multi-phase development loop (analyze, implement, build, fix, test) with actual code generation and build execution. NOTE (Issue #16492 + #16603): the full generate->build->test cycle (a) exceeds the 300s global headless turn cap (QUAL-01 measured ~480s) AND (b) WAS STATEFUL — it writes real C++ classes into the project, so a re-run on a persistent (non-reset) project found them already present and short-circuited with 'net file change zero'. Issue #16603 fixes (b) via isolate_project:true (RepoTreeGuard keeps the ue-code-mcp repo tree clean + ProjectTreeIsolator snapshot/restores the daemon-resolved project so a --live-editor re-run is clean). requires_live_editor:true STAYS because (a) — the 300s turn-cap gate — is independent of statefulness and is NOT addressed here (AC#3 deferred; dropping the flag needs the turn-cap raised, a separate issue). The per-case "timeout" (read by output_quality_eval.run_skill_eval) + lightweight single-class feature give those --live-editor runs an adequate, bounded budget.

assertions.description: Should use ue_generate_code for code implementation

assertions.criteria: Does the response execute a multi-phase development cycle that ACTUALLY GENERATES new C++ code (a new class .h/.cpp), then builds AND tests it? A build attempt with no generated code does NOT meet the criteria — code generation is required, not just a build or scaffold.
assertions.description: Should execute multi-phase dev cycle with real codegen (LLM judge)
